newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates low amid good supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates low amid good supply.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates remained at Thursday's lower levels on Friday, but activity increased as banks sought more call money loans for regular end-of-week tax payments, dealers said.
"Liquidity is still high but banks wanted to make sure there won't be any weekend surprises. So they sought call money loans to last over Saturday and Sunday," one dealer said.
She put fresh settlements at 31 million kuna and said there was still a surplus of some 80 million kuna.

Call money accounted for 28.5 million kuna, granted at a low 7.0 percent. The rate dropped from the usual 8.0 percent on Thursday. "There is good interest from lenders so banks were willing to grant funds at lower prices," the dealer said.
Smaller term loans were struck at 7.0 percent for one-week funds and 10 percent for two-week money.
Delears said they expected liquidity to remain high next week, as the central bank announced it would hold an auction for the purchase of hard currency.
Banks had 30.5 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from 10.5 million on Thursday evening.
There was no overnight trade as no banks reported shortfalls. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
